transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 774 Sweeney Park Lane?
Yes, this is 774 Sweeney Park Lane. I’m here with my father—he’s in a manual wheelchair and can’t leave alone.
Thank you for confirming your address and situation. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
There are two people here — my father, who’s in a manual wheelchair, and me. I’m the one answering.

Thank you for sharing that information. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
Yes, my father can’t leave alone—he uses a manual wheelchair. It doesn’t have a motor.
I heard you mentioned your father and his wheelchair. Who is it that can't leave on their own, and what do they need to get out?
My father can’t leave on his own—he needs his manual wheelchair to get out.
I heard you need help getting your father out. Is there water inside the home right now?
No, there’s no water inside the home. But my father needs a manual wheelchair to get out, and I can’t leave him alone.
I hear your concern about your father needing help. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
No, we don’t have a high-clearance truck, boat, or any free seats in a vehicle. My father needs a manual wheelchair to get out, and we can’t leave him alone.

I hear you’re concerned about your father’s mobility and safety. Let me read that back: 2 people; father needs help leaving because of manual wheelchair; father needs help leaving because of his manual wheelchair; father needs help leaving because of a manual wheelchair to get out; no water inside yet. Is that right?

Yes, that’s right — two people, my father needs help leaving because of his manual wheelchair, no water inside yet.  
*(corrects themselves)*  
Actually, he needs help leaving because he uses a manual wheelchair — not because of a wheelchair to get out.

Thank you for confirming and correcting the details. I've recorded that you need help leaving. No responder has been assigned yet. If water is rising inside, move to the highest floor and call 911 if you can get through. Goodbye.
